name: Video Spectral Coherence
description: Measures spectral coherence between consecutive frames — AI-generated videos show distinct spectral jumps.
mechanism:
This method analyzes spectral coherence across video frame regions for deepfake detection:

1. **Regional Spectral Analysis**: The spatial frequency spectrum is computed independently for multiple regions: face, background, clothing, hair. Each region's spectral characteristic — spectral slope, cutoff frequency, spectral peaks — is measured.

2. **Cross-Region Spectral Coherence**: All regions captured through the same optical system should show coherent spectral characteristics — same noise spectrum, same spectral cutoff (determined by the lens MTF), same compression artifacts. The method checks cross-region spectral coherence. Deepfake composites show spectral incoherence between generated face and captured background.

3. **Spectral Noise Floor Matching**: The spectral noise floor (high-frequency baseline noise level) should be uniform across the frame. The method compares noise floors between regions — different noise floors indicate content from different imaging/generation pipelines.

4. **Spectral Transition Analysis**: At region boundaries (face-background border), the spectral transition should be smooth. The method analyzes spectral characteristics across boundaries — abrupt spectral changes at the face border (changing noise spectrum, changing spectral slope) indicate compositing.

5. **Temporal Spectral Coherence**: The spectral relationship between regions should remain stable over time. The method tracks inter-region spectral ratios — temporal variation in the face-to-background spectral ratio indicates the face content varies independently from the background, consistent with deepfake generation.
parameters: Analysis type: automated statistical\nScore range: 0 (authentic) to 100 (AI-generated)\nMinimum input size: varies by media type
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy depending on input quality and method combination.
source: Based on peer-reviewed research in digital forensics and AI content detection.
useCase: Used as part of multi-signal analysis pipeline to detect AI-generated content.
strengths:
• Research-backed methodology
• Fast computation time
• Complementary to other detection methods
• Works across different AI generators
limitations: • Accuracy varies with input quality\n• Best used in combination with other methods\n• May require calibration for new AI models
